Canada Reminds International Students to Check Study Permit Work Conditions

Overview of IRCC Guidance

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has issued a reminder regarding employment rules for international students in Canada. According to the agency's public statements, holding a study permit does not automatically grant permission to take a job. Students must verify that their individual document explicitly authorizes on-campus or off-campus work before accepting any employment.

Key Employment Rules and Limits

Based on the reported guidance, students who are eligible to work off campus must adhere to specific hour limits while classes are in session.

  • Permit Conditions: Employment is only permitted if explicitly stated on the study permit.
  • Hour Restrictions: Eligible students may work up to 24 hours per week off campus during academic sessions.
  • Post-Graduation Work: Graduates applying for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) may have specific provisions allowing them to work full-time while awaiting a decision, provided they met prior study and work eligibility criteria.

Risks of Non-Compliance

IRCC highlighted that exceeding permitted work hours or working without authorization constitutes a breach of study permit conditions. Reported consequences include:

  • Loss of student status.
  • Refusal of future study or work permit applications.
  • Potential removal from Canada.
  • Broader risks associated with unauthorized labor, including potential records of non-compliance.

Verification and Official Resources

Prospective and current international students are advised to consult official channels to verify permit conditions, tuition requirements, and immigration policies. Exact institutional policies, program structures, and application steps vary by designated learning institution (DLI).

To review official policies and verify announcements, applicants should consult the official IRCC website. Admission, scholarships, and visas are never guaranteed and depend entirely on individual assessments by Canadian immigration authorities and educational institutions.
